title: Reject Boolean endpoint IDs in an opt-in bit export boundary (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Changing only `final[0]` from integer `1` to JSON `true` in the retained PR589 bit word passes the full symbolic checker and the actual `integer-xor-scatter-v1` checked exporter. All 27,234 binary records and 636 frame descriptions remain byte-identical, but the exported final-state Boolean fails the retained native consumer's integer/JSON terminal comparison.

This adds one isolated, source-pinned audit and opt-in `typed-endpoints-integer-xor-v1` wrapper in `research/bit-endpoint-frame-types/`. It requires exact integer endpoint IDs, correct array lengths and in-range frames before delegating to the unchanged integer-label/XOR exporter. The baseline and a valid cancelling scatter pair preserve all three export artifacts byte for byte.

The initial-only Boolean fixture is a nonfailing consumer control: the actual staging script normalizes initial IDs with `int(v)`. The final-ID witness is the demonstrated mismatch. The compiled C++ probe executes the exact terminal predicate against the pinned JSON header and baseline-declared integer final state; it is **not a full native execution**.

This is a finite representation-boundary audit and opt-in repair. No new κ, supplier admission, selected-frontier change or modification of frozen predecessors.

## Task and overlap

- Priority revision 7; task `supplier-boundary-audit`, drawn on the adversarial-audit track. [Task card](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6e761c6152b010f0c93553b1d9d1581d4a6f2c1f/research/bit-endpoint-frame-types/TASK.json).
- Scope **changed** from four-provider admission to a concrete bit exporter contract identified through the card's documented boundary lineage. This tests whether a supplier's accepted representation agrees with its consumer.
- Scientific base `f259dabc7d70e0db8d6d36bfda888f008bbfecc1`; rebased onto refreshed canonical main `4c0a359d88f22f05189d51f48387750b801a45d4`. Guidance, selection and all eleven live inputs were unchanged. [Exact source blobs and SHA256 pins](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/6e761c6152b010f0c93553b1d9d1581d4a6f2c1f/research/bit-endpoint-frame-types/SOURCES.json).
- Nearest predecessors: #2977 / #3801 (scatter mismatch), #2992 (simple-support/snapshot), #3273 / #3004 (XOR/parity), #3100 (integer-label contract), and the retained combined integer-label/XOR wrapper. This adds endpoint-array type/shape/range validation and an actual JSON-consumer predicate witness, preserving those earlier guards.
- Final overlap refresh covered 308 open PRs, 4,339 closed PRs, 4,155 Discussion records and all 6,762 local notes. No same typed-JSON endpoint repair found within that coverage; arbitrary diffs and unpublished work are outside it.
- [Canonical claim and result](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2976#discussioncomment-19140401).

## Validation

Author-checked on Windows with CPython 3.12.0 and MSYS2 GCC 13.1.0:

```sh
python -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-endpoint-frame-types
python -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/bit-endpoint-frame-types
```

The registered replay passes in normal and optimized Python modes, reconstructs all four predecessor export/staging fixtures, and compiles the C++17 terminal-predicate probe. Nine test groups pass under optimized Python with warnings treated as errors. Controls include malformed types/shapes/ranges, all seven delegate-file corruptions, input replacement after validation, existing-output preservation, fractional labels, wrong integer geometry and wrong integer final semantics.

Committed-byte preflight and the official export integrity check pass for all 20 declared files. The Git-free exported package also passes optimized replay and all nine test groups, leaving its 21 files (including the integrity manifest) unchanged. That replay used commit `4d332d095f7bc29669fb6a39bbbc254c230c961f`; the final commit only refreshes README/task-card coordination data, and the final committed-byte/export checks were rerun. Hosted [Registered research packages CI](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39918584806) also passed on Linux for head `6e761c6152b010f0c93553b1d9d1581d4a6f2c1f`: onboarding helper tests, the explicit package replay, and the committed-inputs-unchanged check.

Not run: full native legality/columns, nonempty ownership/banks, physical hosting, precision/tapes, all-size transfer, complete selected cold replay, or optional full-history ancestry preflight (shallow checkout). No independent human or proof-kernel review claimed. The inherited final output copy is not transactional.

Full attribution and limits are in the package README. Prepared by Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in investigation, implementation, testing and writing. New work is Apache-2.0; frozen sources and notices are unchanged.

## Open next questions

Review the four fixtures, then consider adopting the exact-integer endpoint contract in a separately versioned, named producer/consumer pair and running that supplier's complete native/ownership/hosting verification. The next useful step is integration and complete supplier verification, rather than another Boolean-value census.
